title: IDF Strikes Kill 33+ in Gaza City — Last Operating Restaurant and Market Hit
detail: Israeli airstrikes on Gaza City on May 8, 2026 killed at least 33 Palestinians, including a strike that hit the last operating restaurant in Gaza City and a simultaneous strike on a crowded nearby market. The strikes represented one of the highest single-day death tolls since the October 10, 2025 ceasefire. The Times of Israel liveblog confirmed multiple strikes across Gaza City on May 8. The Jerusalem Post reported IDF strikes killed four people including a journalist, whom the IDF claimed was a Hamas member. Gaza's Government Media Office and Al Jazeera correspondents on the ground reported the broader toll of 33+ across multiple locations in Gaza City. The wave of strikes brought the cumulative Palestinian death toll since the October 2025 ceasefire to approximately 870+. Palestinian civil defence teams evacuated casualties to Shifa, Ahli, and Nasser hospitals. The strikes coincided with Israeli cabinet deliberations over resuming full-scale military operations in Gaza after Hamas refused to engage on the five-stage disarmament roadmap demanded by the Board of Peace.

media.caption: IDF strikes kill 33+ in Gaza City on May 8, hitting last operating restaurant and market — ceasefire death toll surpasses 870

title: IDF Strike Kills Son of Hamas Chief Negotiator Khalil Al-Hayya in Gaza City
detail: An Israeli airstrike on May 8, 2026 killed a son of senior Hamas negotiator Khalil Al-Hayya in Gaza City. The Times of Israel reported the killing under the headline 'Son of Hamas's chief negotiator Khalil al-Hayya said killed in IDF strike on Gaza City.' Israel stated the target was an armed operative. The killing came two days after Azzam Al-Hayya — another son of Khalil Al-Hayya — was wounded in a May 6 Israeli strike, marking the fifth time a member of the Hamas chief negotiator's immediate family has been harmed by Israeli fire since the October 2025 ceasefire. Khalil Al-Hayya is Hamas's principal negotiating figure in the disarmament talks with the Board of Peace, making the recurring targeting of his family a significant dimension of the conflict. Hamas condemned the strike as a deliberate assassination targeting the family of a diplomatic representative. The incident drew international condemnation and further complicated ceasefire negotiations already at full impasse.

media.caption: Son of Hamas chief negotiator Khalil al-Hayya killed in IDF strike on Gaza City — fifth family member harmed since Oct 2025 ceasefire

title: Israeli Settler Uses Vehicle to Block Palestinian Ambulance Transporting Critically Ill Patient in West Bank
detail: Video footage published on May 8, 2026 and confirmed by the Times of Israel showed an Israeli settler using his vehicle to physically block a Palestinian ambulance from transporting a critically ill patient on a West Bank road south of Nablus. The ambulance, transporting a patient requiring urgent medical care, was forced to stop while the settler's vehicle blocked the road. The incident added to a documented pattern of settler harassment of Palestinian medical and emergency services. IDF Central Command Chief Maj. Gen. Avi Bluth, who on May 1 had publicly labeled settler violence 'Jewish terror,' was informed of the incident. Rights groups B'Tselem and Médecins Sans Frontières documented similar incidents throughout 2025–2026. OCHA has previously reported that ambulance obstruction by settlers is a 'systemic' problem in parts of the West Bank. The incident came as 2026 settler violence injuries tracked at 360+ Palestinians through early May — the highest pace since records began.

media.caption: Israeli settler blocks Palestinian ambulance in West Bank — footage published May 8, 2026

title: Israeli Cabinet Convenes to Discuss Resuming Full-Scale Gaza War as Hamas Refuses Disarmament
detail: Israel's security cabinet met on or around May 8, 2026 to formally deliberate over the option of resuming full-scale military operations in Gaza after Hamas categorically refused the five-stage disarmament roadmap demanded by the Board of Peace. The Times of Israel reported: 'Ministers set to discuss renewing Gaza war as Hamas refuses to disarm.' The cabinet debate represented the most concrete step yet toward ending the October 10, 2025 ceasefire — now seven months old. Ministers representing the far-right bloc (Ben-Gvir, Smotrich) have consistently argued for war resumption. Finance Minister Smotrich characterized the ceasefire as 'providing cover for Hamas to regroup.' Defense Minister Katz argued renewed military action was inevitable if the disarmament impasse persisted. The Board of Peace High Representative Nickolay Mladenov, in a briefing to the UN Security Council on May 8, warned that the window for a negotiated solution was 'rapidly closing' — but still urged restraint and a diplomatic path. Israel's military posture has shifted: the IDF now controls approximately 60% of Gaza territory, including the buffer zone and the entire Philadelphi Corridor.

media.caption: Israeli cabinet debates resuming Gaza war as Hamas refuses disarmament — security cabinet meeting convened May 8, 2026
